pages.name: One feature file doubled in size and a fixed 200-feature limit turned it into a global 5xx event

elements.text: One feature file doubled in size and a fixed 200-feature
limit turned it into a global 5xx event
The failure was in the ingestion of Cloudflare’s own generated
configuration, not in the traffic that configuration governs.
NORMAL · CHANGE DEPLOYED
Database access control
change deployed
CRITICAL · IMPACT STARTS
First errors observed on
customer HTTP traffic
DEGRADED · MAIN IMPACT ENDS
Correct configuration file
deployed globally
RECOVERED · ALL RESOLVED
All downstream services
restarted and restored
TRIGGER
A change to one of Cloudflare’s database
systems’ permissions made the query output
duplicate entries into the feature file.
MECHANISM
The file doubled in size and passed the
bots module’s preallocated limit of 200
features, against roughly 60 then in use.
SCOPE
Core CDN and security services, Turnstile,
Workers KV, Dashboard, Email Security and
Access were affected, in different ways.
RECOVERY
Core traffic was largely flowing as normal
by 14:30, and all remaining services were
restored at 17:06.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”. All times UTC.

pages.name: The same bad file produced errors on the new proxy and silent false positives on the old one

elements.text: The same bad file produced errors on the new proxy and
silent false positives on the old one
Unrelated to this incident, customer traffic was being migrated to a new proxy version, FL2.
Both versions were affected by the bad feature file, but the impact each one produced differed.
FL2 · THE NEW PROXY ENGINE
HTTP 5xx errors
Customers deployed on the new FL2 proxy
engine observed HTTP 5xx errors for any
traffic that depended on the bots module.
This also affected Workers KV and Access,
which rely on the core proxy.
FL · THE PREVIOUS PROXY ENGINE
Silent bot-score failure
Customers on the old FL engine did not see
errors, but bot scores were not generated
correctly and all traffic received a bot
score of zero.
Customers with rules that block bots would
have seen large numbers of false positives.
Customers who were not using the bot score in their rules did not see any impact.
Observed fact: both proxy behaviours are stated in the published account; neither is inferred here.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”, request-path section. All times UTC.

pages.name: The error rate rose and fell every five minutes until every database node produced the bad file

elements.text: The error rate rose and fell every five minutes until
every database node produced the bad file
NORMAL
CRITICAL
DEGRADED
RECOVERED
First customer errors observed
The feature file was regenerated every five minutes by a query on a ClickHouse cluster that was being gradually updated, so each
cycle could produce either a good or a bad file — until every ClickHouse node generated the bad file and the failure stabilised.
Schematic reconstruction from the published account, not the original monitoring record. No error-rate magnitude is published.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”. Severity bands are this review’s reading of the published status column.

pages.name: Detection took three minutes; identifying the failing module took two hours and fifty-three

elements.text: Detection took three minutes; identifying the failing
module took two hours and fifty-three
AUTOMATED DETECTION
3 min
11:28 impact starts to 11:31, the first automated
test that detects the issue.
TIME TO IDENTIFY THE FAILING MODULE
2 h 53 min
11:31 detection to 14:24, when Bot Management
was identified as the source of the 500 errors.
THE FAILURE ALTERNATED
The system failed and then recovered as
good and bad files alternated every five
minutes — behaviour the published account
calls very unusual for an internal error.
THE STATUS PAGE WENT DOWN TOO
Cloudflare’s status page, hosted
completely off Cloudflare’s
infrastructure with no dependencies on
it, went down at the same time. The
published account calls this a
coincidence.
RECENT DDoS ACTIVITY
In the internal incident chat room the
team was concerned this might continue
the recent spate of high-volume Aisuru
DDoS attacks.
Inferred sequence: the attack hypothesis is what the published account says the team held at the time. Naming it here is not a
criticism of holding it, and the account is explicit that no cyber attack or malicious activity was involved.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”, incident timeline and status-page section. All times UTC.

pages.name: A query that filtered on table name but not database name became an unhandled panic in the core proxy

elements.text: A query that filtered on table name but not database
name became an unhandled panic in the core proxy
Access change
made explicit
Query returns
duplicate rows
Feature file
doubles in size
200-feature
limit exceeded
Thread panics,
5xx returned
THE QUERY
SELECT
name,
type
FROM system.columns
WHERE table = 'http_requests_features'
order by name;
The feature-file query filtered on the table name but
not the database name, so after the 11:05 change made
access to the r0 database explicit it returned columns twice.
THE LIMIT
thread fl2_worker_thread panicked:
called Result::unwrap() on an Err value
The bots module preallocates memory for at most 200
features, well above the roughly 60 in use. The oversized
file hit that limit and the check produced an unhandled error.
Observed facts: the access change, the query form, the file growth and the 200-feature limit are each stated in the published
account. The order that connects them into one chain is that account’s own inferred sequence.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”, query-behaviour-change and memory-preallocation sections.

pages.name: Four conditions had to hold at once, and no single one of them is the cause

elements.text: Four conditions had to hold at once, and no
single one of them is the cause
TECHNICAL
An assumption about the query’s scope was never restated
The feature-generation query assumed table metadata would only ever be returned for the
default database. That assumption was not revisited when the permissions model changed at 11:05.
TECHNICAL
A fixed limit guarded memory but had no bounded failure path
The bots module preallocates memory for at most 200 machine-learning features. An input above
that limit produced an unhandled error and a thread panic, not a rejected file or a degraded score.
PROCEDURAL
Cloudflare-generated configuration was trusted more than user input
The first published remediation item is to harden ingestion of Cloudflare-generated configuration
files in the same way as user-generated input — which states that, before this incident, it was not.
PROCEDURAL
The change propagated gradually, so the failure looked like an attack
Only the updated part of the ClickHouse cluster produced bad data, so output alternated every
five minutes and the failure signature resembled an attack rather than a deployment.
Each factor traces to the timeline evidence on slides 6 and 7, and no single one of them is described here as the cause.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”, query-behaviour, memory-preallocation and remediation sections.

pages.name: Rapid global propagation of internally generated configuration is the condition both 2019 and 2025 share

elements.text: Rapid global propagation of internally generated
configuration is the condition both 2019 and 2025 share
SYSTEMIC CONDITION
Internally generated configuration reaches every machine in minutes
Both outages began inside Cloudflare’s own configuration path, and in both the step that made a local
defect global was the same. Naming that shared condition is an inference across two published accounts.
2 July 2019
TRIGGER
A new WAF managed rule containing a regular expression
that backtracked enormously and exhausted CPU worldwide.
PROPAGATION
Pushed through Quicksilver, which distributes changes
globally in seconds; by design the WAF skipped the
staged rollout process.
MITIGATION
A global kill switch — a “global terminate” — executed
at 14:07; traffic and CPU normal again by 14:09.
TIME TO RECOVERY
27 minutes
18 November 2025
TRIGGER
A database permissions change that made the Bot
Management feature file more than double in size.
PROPAGATION
The feature file is refreshed every few minutes and
published to the entire network so the model can react
to new bots and new bot attacks.
MITIGATION
No per-feature kill switch is described; the remediation
commits to enabling more global kill switches.
TIME TO RECOVERY
5 h 38 min
The published account calls this Cloudflare’s worst outage since 2019, and the first in six-plus years to stop most core traffic.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”, and “Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019”. All times UTC.

pages.name: Three controls limited the damage and are the ones to protect

elements.text: Three controls limited the damage
and are the ones to protect
PROTECT THIS
Automated detection
was fast
The first automated test detected
the issue at 11:31, three minutes
after impact began at 11:28. Manual
investigation started the following
minute and the incident call was
created at 11:35.
PROTECT THIS
A bypass existed
and was used
At 13:05, internal system bypasses
failed Workers KV and Cloudflare
Access back to a prior version of
the core proxy, reducing impact for
every downstream system — before
the trigger was known.
PROTECT THIS
The older engine
degraded, not failed
Customers on the old FL proxy
engine did not see errors, and
customers who were not using the
bot score in their rules saw no
impact at all.
Observed facts from the published account; the judgement that these three are worth protecting is this review’s.
Cloudflare, “Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025”, incident timeline and other-impact section. All times UTC.

pages.name: Five questions the published account does not settle

elements.text: Five questions the published account does not settle
When did impact begin — 11:20 or 11:28?
The opening paragraph states the network began experiencing significant failures at 11:20; the incident timeline records
impact starts at 11:28. This deck uses 11:28 for every derived duration and says so on each page that shows one.
When was the Workers KV bypass effective — 13:04, 13:05 or 13:10?
The narrative gives 13:04 for the patch and 13:10 for restoration, while the timeline gives 13:05 for the bypass. Three
values describe one mitigation, and the published account does not reconcile them.
What did the outage cost?
No error count, request volume, affected-customer count, availability figure or financial figure appears anywhere in the
published account. NO DATA.
Who owns the four corrective actions, and by when?
No owner, target date or verification method is published for any of the four remediation items. NO DATA.
Do other core proxy modules share the unbounded failure pattern?
The account commits to reviewing failure modes for error conditions across all core proxy modules, but does not say
whether any others were found. Unconfirmed.
Each item names the evidence that would settle it. None is resolved here by inference. Cloudflare, 18 November 2025 account.
